title: When No One Is Asking
statement: A self assembles in the interval before performance: an ancient face held between the city’s demands and a botanical interior, with Earth, bird, and impossible menagerie as quiet witnesses. The collage treats identity not as an answer but as a habitat—growing, observing, and remaining briefly unobserved.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent yourself when no one is asking anything of you.

notes.note: Build a layered self-portrait: an urban memory as ground, a botanical presence as a living silhouette, the bronze portrait as the central self, and an isolated Earth and flamingo as distant inner symbols.

The central bust reads clearly as an unprompted self, while the city, plant, Earth, and flamingo establish public life, growth, distance, and instinct. I’ll add one restrained archival image as a private symbolic halo, then name the work.

notes.note: The canvas now has a legible self-portrait structure: the bust is the quiet center, the botanical plate acts as an inner body, the city supplies social pressure, and the distant Earth and flamingo open the field of thought. I’ll make one subtle adjustment so the menagerie reads more clearly as a halo behind the head, then review the result before finishing.

The final canvas is visually resolved: the bronze head anchors the composition, botanical growth and the archival menagerie form an inner halo, while the city, flamingo, and Earth create a quiet orbit of public and private selves. The title and statement are present and nonblank.
